review_scope: Targeted source review, not a systematic literature review. No claim of first discovery or field validation.

cases.title: Holuhraun: volcanic terrain for Mars mobility
cases.question: Can a basaltic field support terrain-navigation trials relevant to Elysium Planitia?
cases.novelty_finding: Voigt et al. (2025) explicitly compare Holuhraun and Elysium Planitia. The RAVEN project also documents exploration research here. This app contributes an auditable comparison, not discovery of the analog.
cases.interpretation: The literature supports the volcanic-process analogy. Use the regional terrain scores to shortlist navigation exercises, then survey the actual traverse. A regional DEM does not resolve wheel-scale obstacles.
limits: Elysium is outside the mobility profile's published Jezero/Gale reference set: this is an exploratory application of the same weights.
The annual precipitation proxy is about 1332 mm: Holuhraun is not a hyperarid Martian climate substitute.
Lava morphology, eruption scale, gravity and atmospheric conditions differ; an Earth field trial cannot qualify flight hardware.
cases.stress_reason: Does the site's position depend primarily on broad terrain rather than geological or environmental agreement? Remaining features are renormalized; this is a diagnostic, not an improved score.
field_plan: Survey a permitted traverse with photogrammetry and record wheel-scale rock size and slope distributions.
Measure slip and navigation error on specified terrain classes using a repeatable rover protocol.
Document seasonal water/snow and compare the field patch with the regional sampling window.

cases.title: Undara: a cave-robotics research lead
cases.question: Which terrestrial cave properties could support a lunar subsurface robotics experiment?
cases.novelty_finding: Queensland Parks documents the lava-tube system and sediment-covered cave floors. This targeted review does not establish a first use for lunar robotics. A comprehensive literature search and site-authority review are still required.
cases.interpretation: Basaltic cave morphology motivates a robotics investigation. Regional surface terrain and climate are not measurements of the cave interior, entrance geometry, radio propagation or traversability.
limits: The Earth thermal input is modeled mean annual air temperature, not a measured cave temperature.
The lunar ~290 K input describes a modeled permanently shadowed cave environment; it is not a direct subsurface temperature measurement or proof of a traversable tube.
Regional woodland, cave sediment, Earth gravity and atmosphere differ from lunar conditions. Access and conservation requirements must be confirmed.
cases.stress_reason: Test whether the comparison remains useful without comparing regional Earth air temperature with a modeled lunar cave environment. Remaining features are renormalized.
field_plan: Obtain permission for a non-invasive cave survey and define a specific test chamber.
Log interior temperature through time; survey entrance geometry and obstacle sizes rather than inferring them from a regional DEM.
Test localization drift and communications loss with a repeatable, conservation-compatible robotics protocol.

cases.title: Svalbard: polar operations with explicit limits
cases.question: Can an established Arctic analog inform a limited polar-prospecting field exercise?
cases.novelty_finding: NASA and ESA document AMASE campaigns in Svalbard. The Bockfjord volcanic centers are described in the 2011 LPI analog-sites workshop. These sources establish prior analog use, not validation for lunar resource extraction.
cases.interpretation: Cold terrain and permafrost proxies motivate field-procedure tests. Permafrost probability is not water-ice concentration, mineable inventory or evidence that Earth material reproduces lunar regolith.
limits: The modeled permafrost probability is a regional proxy; it is not a borehole measurement of ice at this sampling point.
Shackleton's representative region is not an approved base or a uniform resource deposit. Permanent shadow and cryogenic vacuum are not reproduced in Svalbard.
Hydrothermal alteration, terrestrial biology and protection requirements limit geological and operational transfer.
cases.stress_reason: Reveal dependence on the strongest resource-related proxy. A changed rank measures assumption sensitivity, not confirmation or rejection of lunar resource suitability.
field_plan: Review existing AMASE work and identify a distinct procedure to test before proposing new field activity.
Use permitted non-invasive geophysics and independent ground-temperature observations to check the regional proxy.
Document contamination controls and compare sampling procedures without claiming lunar ice-extraction equivalence.
